- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overreacting to sentiment-driven momentum.
- If sentiment turns negative (e.g., <0.3) and forecast is still trending up, adjust downward by 3–8% to reflect risk-off behavior.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs; if last 3–5 prices are rising, cap forecast peak at 1.5x recent high to prevent lagged overcorrection.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating +/– 0.3–0.6), apply mean reversion bias: forecast should revert to 20–30-day moving average within 3–5 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from forecast in first 5 days, reduce subsequent forecast slope by 20–30% to account for lagged market adjustment.
- If sentiment is consistently low (e.g., <0.2) and forecast is high, apply downward bias of 5–10% to reflect subdued market participation.
- When sentiment spikes +0.5+ and forecast is flat, initiate upward correction by 3–5% to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
